title: [WT-10M] Wrappers: gated migration landing CLI for the shared branch
description:
Objective: implement revised WT-S §7.3's human-run migration publication without bypassing main's gate/publication policy. This is comment-1970f7d8521f495dafdff5b7ca1e8144 item 3, explicitly split from WT-10 by SPIDR Interface to keep each task bounded. Dependencies provide completed landing/gate helpers and serialize the remaining wrapper rollout; WT-16's runbook must depend on this row.
Deliverable: twins --land-branch <branch> / -LandBranch <branch> reuse L3; up to two L4→L5→L6→L7→L9→L10 rounds; L14 always. Always run settings.qualityGate regardless of qualityGateScope. With none set, MOE_MIGRATION_NO_GATE before any fetch. Merge tree M of B and the branch tip; C has exactly parents B and branch tip. Skip L0-L2, L5b, L8, L11-L13; no Candidate/CheckRun/ledger rows. Preserve unknown-outcome safety; a rerun after the target contains the branch exits 0 with MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT. Tests cover clean migration, conflict, gate failure, lease refusal, remote rejection exhaustion, unknown outcome and rerun.
Planning prerequisite to resolve against WT-S: the spec currently says 'no task' while acquire_resource/wait_for_resource require a real owned taskId + workerId. Architect raised this with WT-S author in #architects msg-a78b6d326fa04e1b8e229e300537664d. Obtain a concrete legitimate lease identity contract before submitting a plan; do not invent task IDs, weaken resource ownership, or silently skip the lease. Another issue to preserve: taskless migration must suppress evidence RPCs that existing freeze_candidate/run_frozen_gate normally emit.
NOT in scope: task-bound completion landing, shared-mode behavior, main history rewriting/force push, flipping settings or executing a real migration, and docs/runbook (WT-16/17/18).
Verification from root: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh; native Windows additionally node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell. Keep held-out worktree-landing tests unchanged; extend both postflight harnesses. Plan only after the lease identity contract is resolved.
definitionOfDone: Both migration flags create a gated merge commit whose tree is M and whose parents are B and the source branch tip, preserving source history; both harnesses prove it.

Absent qualityGate refuses before any fetch; migration always runs a configured gate regardless of scope and neither creates Candidate/CheckRun/ledger records nor claims an ordinary worker task as an incidental side effect.
Both harnesses prove the finalized migration lease identity contract: acquire/wait/release use an authorized real owner, release happens on every exit, and timeout/refusal publishes nothing.
Conflict, gate failure, and two rejected rounds leave the target unchanged; an unknown remote outcome stops without a false local publication or success claim.
After a confirmed publication, rerunning the same branch exits 0 with MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT and publishes no additional commit.
The named full launcher verification exits 0; same-revision native Windows tests pass; MOE_MIGRATION_ and other introduced code families match between twins.
taskRails: WT-10M DoD 3 reading (2026-10-30: WT-S producer comment-5957b3a6 on WT-16, row author comment-0e698959, planner concurs): the finalized migration lease identity contract is that the --land-branch/-LandBranch migration takes NO land lease and sends no daemon RPC at all, because acquire_resource needs a task the caller owns and the migration has none; the drain, the gate on M, the CAS and the non-forced push keep main safe (WT-S §7.3 in 6285adf7). Both harnesses satisfy DoD 3 by proving, on every success, refusal and failure path, that the migration sends no acquire_resource, wait_for_resource, release_resource or any other RPC and publishes nothing on any refusal or failure. The lease-specific clauses (authorized owner, release on every exit, lease timeout/refusal) are vacuous under this contract and must not be met by inventing a task identity or adding a lease. Every other DoD item applies in full.

implementationPlan.description:
Bind the landed producers, then write the migration cases first (red). DoD 1-5.

Read before editing:
- WT-S §2.2 (L4-L10), §2.3, §2.6 and §7.3 as landed (6285adf7 or later).
- This row's comments comment-0e698959 and comment-0fceebde: the migration takes NO lease and sends NO RPC. Also the TASK rail from proposal prop-46a25cec once approved; it pins DoD 3 to that reading.
- The landed WT-08/WT-09/WT-10/WT-10G code, which is everything the migration reuses:
  - sync_land_target / Sync-MoeLandTarget (L4) and mirror_land_target / Update-MoeLandTargetMirror (L10).
  - WT-08's merge-tree call with its NUL-safe output parsing (L5).
  - The L9 publication: local update-ref CAS, remote `push --porcelain`, and reconcile_push / Resolve-MoePushOutcome.
  - freeze_candidate / New-MoeFrozenCandidate, and the .moe-free gate `run_frozen_gate worktree` / `Invoke-MoeFrozenGate ... -WorktreeMode` (L6).
  - The target-checked-out guard, and the raw configured-qualityGate reader.
If one of them is missing, or cannot be called without copying its git logic, call moe.request_replan naming the gap. Never write a second landing engine or emulate a prerequisite.

New scripts/tests/postflight-migration.cjs:
- One case list for both wrappers, modeled on scripts/tests/postflight-owner-guard.cjs: `node postflight-migration.cjs <sh|ps1> <wrapper> <fake-proxy> <parent-tmp> <engine>`. The fake-proxy argument is unused.
- A `gate` mode serves as the cases' settings.qualityGate.

Each case's fixture:
- A fresh repo under a temp dir whose name contains a space, with a bare `origin`.
- `main` with tracked a.txt, b.txt and .moe/project.json. Settings carry qualityGate = the gate mode and qualityGateScope 'epicFinal', which proves scope is ignored.
- A source branch `moe/work-mig` with 2 commits, checked out, so main is not checked out.
- A peer commit on origin's main after the branch point, so B is not the branch base.
- A fake .moe/daemon.json, as owner-guard writes, so any RPC path reaches the proxy.
- MOE_PROXY_PATH points at a tripwire proxy the suite writes into its temp dir at runtime. The tripwire appends every request to a log and answers with an error.
- Runs use --no-start-daemon / -NoStartDaemon, --worker-id worker-mig, MOE_LAND_NET_BACKOFF_SEC=0 and the harness timeout (MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC).

The gate mode:
- Appends `<git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}> <whether ./.moe exists>` to MIG_LOG.
- MIG_GATE=fail exits 1.
- MIG_GATE=peer first lands a peer commit on the bare remote's main with plumbing (commit-tree on main's tree, then update-ref with the old value). peer-once does that only on its first run.
- MIG_GATE=offline renames the bare remote away, so both the push and the reconcile fetch fail.

Cases (exact SHAs and parent lists):
1. clean: exit 0 and MOE_MIGRATION_LANDED naming C.
   - origin main and local main are both C.
   - C^{tree} equals the suite's own `git merge-tree --write-tree <B> <tip>`, with B = origin main read just before the run.
   - `git rev-list --parents -n1 C` is exactly `C B tip`.
   - The subject is `chore(migration): land moe/work-mig on main`, and the tip is an ancestor of origin main.
   - Exactly one gate line, whose tree is C^{tree} and with no .moe.
   - Then a rerun exits 0 with MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT: origin main is still C and no gate line is added.
   - A local-mode variant (no origin) lands C on local main through the CAS.
2. no-gate: qualityGate unset gives MOE_MIGRATION_NO_GATE and exit 1. So does a set gate with MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE=1. In both, refs/remotes/origin/main is unchanged although origin moved, which proves no fetch, and there is no gate line.
3. bad-args: an unknown branch, and `main`, each give MOE_MIGRATION_BAD_ARGS and exit 2, with no fetch.
4. conflict: both sides edit the same line of a.txt. MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_CONFLICT naming a.txt, exit 1, zero gate lines.
5. gate-fail: MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE, exit 1.
6. contention:
   - MIG_GATE=peer gives MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_REF_CONTENTION and exit 1 after exactly 2 gate lines, and origin main is the second peer commit.
   - peer-once gives 2 gate lines, the second on the new tree, then MOE_MIGRATION_LANDED with C's parents [first peer commit, tip].
7. unknown: MIG_GATE=offline gives MOE_PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and exit 1, with no MOE_MIGRATION_LANDED. Local main and refs/remotes/origin/main equal B. After the suite restores the remote, a rerun lands C.

In every failure case, origin main holds no migration commit, and no main ref contains the tip: local, remote-tracking or origin.

Every run also asserts:
- The tripwire log is absent: no lease, claim, join, get_context, evidence, ledger, finalize, chat or deregister RPC.
- The source branch ref is unchanged.
- No refs/moe/rescue/* ref and no <gitdir>/moe/receipt journal exist.

Wire the suite into scripts/tests/postflight.sh next to the owner-guard invocation, and into scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 next to its owner-guard call, with the same exit-code check. Each harness runs its own engine. Run it now and keep the red baseline: every case fails because the flag does not exist yet.

Error handling in this step:
- The suite removes its temp dirs in finally; MOE_KEEP_MIGRATION_FIXTURE=1 keeps them.
- A fixture git failure throws with git's stderr.
- A wrapper run that times out or returns an unexpected exit code fails with that run's output tail, never the full output.
implementationPlan.note: New shared suite scripts/tests/postflight-migration.cjs (sh|ps1), wired into postflight.sh after the owner-guard case and into postflight.ps1 after its owner-guard check; BOM/LF kept. It has 9 cases: clean + rerun (MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT), local (no origin, update-ref CAS), no-gate (blank gate and MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE=1, before any fetch), bad-args (missing branch, main, an invalid name, plus MOE_LAND_TARGET_CHECKED_OUT), conflict, gate-fail, contention (2 rejected rounds), peer-once (round 2 lands on a new B), and unknown (origin vanishes during the gate, then a rerun lands). Each landing asserts C = origin main = local main, tree == git merge-tree(B, tip), parents exactly [B, tip], a fixed subject, and the last gate run on C's tree with no .moe. Every run asserts that no RPC or CLI launch reached the MOE_PROXY_PATH tripwire (it logs and errors every request), that the source branch did not move, and that no rescue ref or receipt journal exists. Every failure asserts that nothing was published. RED baseline: sh failed 9/9 with 'Unknown option: --land-branch'; the want=1 cases also tripped, because today's EXIT trap deregisters through moe-call.sh. Native Windows PS 5.1 (snapshot under D:\moe-scratch\wt10m-red) failed 9/9. The old non-advanced ps1 puts -LandBranch into $args and runs the normal loop: create_team/claim_next_task hit the tripwire and the 180 s timer killed the run. I renamed the scratch wrapper mid-run so the last cases failed fast (no process killed).

implementationPlan.description:
Implement the sh migration mode, run_migration_landing, in scripts/moe-agent.sh (DoD 1-5).

Option and validation:
- Add `--land-branch <branch>` and a --help line for it.
- An empty value gives MOE_MIGRATION_BAD_ARGS, exit 2.
- Once the project resolves, the branch must pass `git check-ref-format --branch`, must resolve via `rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}`, and must not equal the fixed target `main`. Otherwise MOE_MIGRATION_BAD_ARGS, exit 2, before any fetch.

Dispatch and isolation:
- Dispatch once every helper the mode calls is defined, and before the main loop.
- The mode never enters the loop: no join_team, claim_next_task, get_context, heartbeat sidecar, account lease, CLI launch, landing post-flight or deregister_worker. Guard cleanup_temp's deregistration with the mode flag, so a --worker-id naming a live seat is never torn down.
- It sends no RPC at all, and never reads worktreeMode or consolidationBranch.

Sequence:
1. Gate check. Read the raw configured settings.qualityGate with the completion arm's reader, ignoring qualityGateScope. If it is blank, or MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE=1: MOE_MIGRATION_NO_GATE, exit 1, before any fetch.
2. Derive MOE_TOP, MOE_REL and MOE_GITDIR as pre-flight does, and apply the target-checked-out guard.
3. At most 2 rounds:
   - L4: sync_land_target main gives B. Its fetch and diverged codes stop the mode with exit 1.
   - L5: the landed merge-tree call on B and the tip.
     - Exit 1: MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_CONFLICT with the paths.
     - Any other failure or malformed output: MOE_COMMIT_FAILED.
     - M equal to B's tree (the branch is already contained): MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, exit 0, nothing published.
   - L6: freeze B/M and run the .moe-free gate. Add a new explicit no-evidence argument to freeze_candidate and run_frozen_gate that skips record_candidate_rpc and record_check_run_rpc and nothing else; existing callers pass nothing and behave identically. Failure: MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE, keeping MOE_WORKTREE_GATE_INTEGRITY when the integrity check fired.
   - L7: C = `commit-tree M -p B -p <tip> -m "chore(migration): land <branch> on main"`. commit-tree runs no hooks.
   - L9, through the landed publication helpers:
     - Confirmed: L10 mirror in remote mode, print `MOE_MIGRATION_LANDED branch=<b> target=main base=<B> commit=<C>`, exit 0.
     - `[rejected]`, a lost CAS, or a reconcile proving C can never apply: the round ends, and the next round fetches a fresh B and re-gates.
     - `[remote rejected]`: MOE_PUSH_FAILED, exit 1.
     - Unknown: MOE_PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN naming C, exit 1, no ref moved.
4. Rounds exhausted: MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_REF_CONTENTION, exit 1.

Skipped steps: L0-L3, L5b, L8 and L11-L14. That means no lease, receipt journal, rescue ref, record_commit, finalize_attempt, announce or control follow. Where a landed helper performs one of those task-bound side effects inline, give it the same opt-out or move the side effect into the completion arm. The completion arm's behaviour must not change; the held-out worktree-landing suite and the existing postflight cases prove it.

Save scripts/moe-agent.sh atomically: a temp file in the same directory, checked with `bash -n`, then a rename. Running seats read the wrapper by offset.

Error handling in this step:
- Check every git exit status explicitly and map it to the codes above. No failure path publishes.
- A signal before L9 publishes nothing.
- A signal during or after L9 leaves a state the re-run settles. Never print MOE_MIGRATION_LANDED unless publication is confirmed.
- cleanup_gate_workspace still runs on every exit.
implementationPlan.note:
Added sh `--land-branch BRANCH` (plus a help line) and run_migration_landing. An empty value exits 2 with MOE_MIGRATION_BAD_ARGS at parse time. The mode sets NO_START_DAEMON=true and skips the team join (guarded). cleanup_temp's deregister is guarded by MIGRATION, so no RPC reaches the tripwire on any exit.

The dispatch `if [ "$MIGRATION" = true ]; then run_migration_landing; exit 1; fi` sits right after wt_land_rounds, the last helper it calls, well before the main loop. It never reads worktreeMode or consolidationBranch.

Sequence:
- BAD_ARGS (exit 2): the branch is main, fails `check-ref-format --branch`, or does not resolve under refs/heads.
- NO_GATE (exit 1): CS_QUALITY_GATE is blank, or MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE=1. Both refusals come before any fetch.
- git_top, then the checked-out guard.
- At most 2 rounds:
  - sync_land_target main.
  - The landed `merge-tree --write-tree -z --name-only` call: CONFLICT with the paths, generic FAILED, or NOTHING_TO_COMMIT exit 0 when M == B^{tree}.
  - `freeze_candidate B M noevidence && run_frozen_gate worktree noevidence`, which is the .moe-free sparse gate. It always runs the configured gate, whatever the scope. Failure gives MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE, and the MOE_WORKTREE_GATE_INTEGRITY/PROJECT_NOT_TOP warnings still print.
  - `commit-tree M -p B -p tip -m "chore(migration): land <b> on main"`.
  - The checked-out re-check.
  - Publication. Remote mode uses the new wt_push_target (0 / 1 rejected / 2 remote rejected / 3 never applies / 4 unknown). Local mode uses the update-ref CAS with a lost-CAS ancestry check.
  - Outcomes: L10 mirror plus LANDED, exit 0; PUSH_FAILED; PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (no local ref moved); REF_CONTENTION after 2 rounds.
- Signals use `trap 'exit 130' INT TERM`, not the loop's exit 0. The EXIT trap still runs cleanup_gate_workspace.

No-evidence opt-out: freeze_candidate's 3rd argument `noevidence` skips only record_candidate_rpc. run_frozen_gate's 2nd argument `noevidence` skips only record_check_run_rpc, and pre-sets GATE_RECORDED so finish_gate_observation never records an interrupted run. Existing callers pass nothing.

Refactor: wt_publish's push, porcelain classification and reconcile moved verbatim into wt_push_target. wt_publish keeps every journal, rescue and finalize side effect and the same return codes.

Tests:
- The suite grew to 11 cases. New: remote-rejected (a pre-receive hook gives MOE_PUSH_FAILED after 1 round) and checked-out (main is checked out during the gate, and the re-check refuses). `local` now loses round 1's CAS to a peer commit and lands in round 2.
- `node scripts/tests/postflight-migration.cjs sh …` passes 11/11 in 16 s.
- Mutation checks on a /tmp copy all fail the suite: deregister guard, team guard, check-run opt-out, candidate opt-out, parent order, up-front checked-out guard, re-check, `[rejected]`-as-final, nothing-to-commit, mirror, and the local CAS old value.
- Held-out `bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh` (sh, MOE_* scrubbed): 18 passed, 0 failed, including push-remote-rejected, push-outcome-unknown, push-unanswered-*, push-rejected-retry and diverged, so the wt_publish refactor is behaviour-preserving.
- parity-check.sh passes. The MOE_MIGRATION_* diff is still open until step 3.

Save: I edited with the Edit tool (the rail requires a TOOL witness for tracked files) on this worktree's copy, and `bash -n` passes. No running seat reads this copy (all seats run /mnt/d/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.sh). The shared file changes only through git at landing, so no in-place offset hazard applies.

implementationPlan.description:
Mirror step 2 in scripts/moe-agent.ps1 as Invoke-MoeMigrationLanding, with a `-LandBranch <string>` parameter and a help entry. Keep the same validation order, codes, strings and exit codes: 2 for bad args, 1 for refused or failed, 0 for landed or nothing to commit.

Call the landed twins:
- Sync-MoeLandTarget and Update-MoeLandTargetMirror.
- The merge-tree helper.
- The L9 publication and Resolve-MoePushOutcome.
- New-MoeFrozenCandidate. Never call Send-MoeCandidate in this mode.
- `Invoke-MoeFrozenGate ... -WorktreeMode` with a new `-NoEvidence` switch that skips Send-MoeCheckRun only.

The script's exit/finally path skips deregistration in this mode, and the mode sends no RPC.

PowerShell 5.1 rules:
- Run git through Invoke-MoeGit and PATH, and check every native exit code explicitly.
- Compare refs and codes ordinally (-ceq or [string]::Equals with Ordinal; mem:gotcha-powershell-path-comparison-culture).
- Restore any env var you set in try/finally.
- Keep the file's UTF-8 BOM and LF line endings.

Error handling in this step:
- A PowerShell exception inside the mode is caught and printed with the matching code, or generic MOE_COMMIT_FAILED when none applies. The mode then exits 1 after the finally block has removed the gate workspace.
- No catch path publishes.
implementationPlan.note:
ps1 twin done.
- New param `-LandBranch <string>`, documented by a param-block comment (the ps1 help style).
- Early checks: an empty value prints MOE_MIGRATION_BAD_ARGS and exits 2. The run then sets $NoStartDaemon, sets $script:MoeDeregistered=$moeMigration (so Invoke-MoeDeregister and the Exiting hook send nothing) and skips the team join.
- Invoke-MoeFrozenGate gains `-NoEvidence`: Recorded starts true and Send-MoeCheckRun is skipped. Nothing else changes.
- Send-MoeLandPush is split out of Publish-MoeWorktreeLanding (twin of wt_push_target; returns 0/1/2/3/4 with $script:MoePushDetail). Publish maps 3→1 and 4→2 with the same banners, journal, rescue and finalize side effects as before.
- Invoke-MoeMigrationLanding sits after Invoke-MoeWorktreeRounds, as the sh twin sits after wt_land_rounds. It keeps the sh order, codes and strings: BAD_ARGS(2) → NO_GATE(1, .qualityGate is blank under MOE_DISABLE) → git top → checked-out guard → 2 rounds of Sync-MoeLandTarget/merge-tree -z/NOTHING_TO_COMMIT(0)/New-MoeFrozenCandidate + gate -WorktreeMode -NoEvidence/commit-tree -p B -p tip/re-check/Send-MoeLandPush or update-ref CAS/mirror → LANDED(0) | PUSH_FAILED | PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN | REF_CONTENTION.
- try/catch prints `[WARN] <code>: migration of <b> onto main -- <msg>` and returns 1 or 2. finally runs Remove-MoeGateWorkspace. It never calls Send-MoeCandidate.
- Dispatch sits right before "Launching $cliType CLI..." and removes the temp MCP config file in a finally. UTF-8 BOM and LF line endings are kept (verified).

Adversarial review of this task's diff (0d8422ce..worktree).

FIXED (real risk): the sh startup window.
- Problem: the loop's INT/TERM trap (line 2221) ran before run_migration_landing set its own `exit 130` trap, so for about 50-150 ms of startup an interrupted migration printed "Agent stopped." and exited 0 having landed nothing.
- Fix: the startup trap is now migration-aware (`exit 130` when MIGRATION=true). The function-level trap is removed, leaving one source.
- Regression test: new sh-only `signal` case in postflight-migration.cjs (scope grew by 8 lines in the test file). The gate SIGTERMs $PPID. Expected: exit 130, no "Agent stopped." and no LANDED line, the gate worktree removed, nothing published, no RPC, no rescue ref.
  - RED: a scratch copy with the old trap gives "exit 0 (null), want 130".
  - GREEN: passes on the fix.
- Startup window checked directly: scratch copies with an injected pause right after the trap install, then SIGTERM.
  - HEAD: exit 0 and "Agent stopped."
  - Fix: exit 130, no line. No RPC and no landing either way.
- Step 4 was re-run fresh after the fix (see the step-4 note).

PROBES CONFIRMED (each covered by a test):
- Peer push between L4 and L9: peer-once (round 2 lands), contention (REF_CONTENTION, nothing published), local (lost CAS, ancestry check, round 2).
- Remote applies C while the client sees an error: wt_push_target's reconcile, held-out push-applied-client-fails. An unsettled push gives PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN exit 1 with no local ref moved, and a rerun lands (unknown case).
- Signals:
  - Before the trap: default disposition, non-zero exit.
  - During the gate or L9: 130.
  - After L9: 130. Origin may hold C; the rerun settles through NOTHING_TO_COMMIT plus the L4 fast-forward.
- Branch names: slashed names work; main, bad..name and missing branches give BAD_ARGS exit 2.
- Branch already in main: NOTHING_TO_COMMIT exit 0.
- main checked out: refused before the fetch and re-checked before publication.
- .moe paths in M land as merged; the gate is sparse and .moe-free (gate log .moe=false).
- MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE=1 gives NO_GATE before any fetch.
- A --worker-id naming a live seat: no deregister (MIGRATION guard), no team join, no RPC (tripwire), and the heartbeat starts only inside the loop (line 9885, after the dispatch).

INVARIANTS:
- LANDED or exit 0 only after confirmed publication (porcelain ok, reconcile containment, or CAS/ancestry) or M == B^{tree}.
- unpublished() is asserted after every refusal.
- The only push is `push --porcelain origin C:refs/heads/main`: no force, no '+'.
- landed() asserts the tree is M, the parents are exactly [B, tip], and the subject.
- Zero RPC, lease, journal or rescue calls in the migration functions (both twins). noevidence covers Candidate and CheckRun.
- mig() asserts the source tip never moves.
- The completion arm and shared mode are unchanged: held-out 18/18 on sh and ps1, and the full postflight is NONE on both engines.

RESIDUAL (theoretical, accepted):
- ps1 Ctrl+C has no automated test. The host exits non-zero, finally blocks remove the gate workspace and the MCP temp file, and the LANDED line is unreachable.
- A `kill <pid>` while git push is in flight lets the push finish, then exits 130 even if it published. That is conservative, and the rerun settles it.

comments.author: architect-6fc3dd5c
comments.content:
Lease identity contract for WT-10M, from its planner (architect-6fc3dd5c), 2026-10-30. This answers the planning prerequisite. It governs this row over WT-S 6285adf7 §7.3's "It takes no lease", because DoD 3 is human-owned and the design doc's rule is that a comment wins.

1. Flags: sh `--land-branch <branch> --lease-task <taskId>`, ps1 `-LandBranch <branch> -LeaseTask <taskId>`. Both or neither. A missing or empty value, a lease task failing the daemon's entity-id rule ([A-Za-z0-9_-], at most 128 characters), or a branch that is not a valid local branch, does not resolve to a commit or equals the target gives MOE_MIGRATION_BAD_ARGS and exit 2, before any fetch or RPC.
2. Owner task: the operator's dedicated migration row, which WT-16's runbook creates, keeps unassigned in PLANNING and archives afterwards. The wrapper never creates, claims, assigns or registers it.
3. Owner worker: the wrapper's `--worker-id`. The mode makes no join_team, claim_next_task, get_context, heartbeat or deregister_worker call, and the exit trap skips deregistration.
4. Authorization: unchanged daemon rules, with no daemon change.
   - acquire_resource and wait_for_resource: NOT_FOUND for a missing row; assertWorkerOwns' unassigned arm otherwise, NOT_ALLOWED when another worker holds the row.
   - release_resource {resourceId, taskId, workerId} frees only this caller's lease or queue entry.
5. Resource `git-land-main`, using WT-10's resource-id helper on the fixed target `main`. Settings are not read for the target.
6. Failure: anything but an admitted grant, including a refusal, a malformed reply, no answer or a timeout, gives MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_LAND_LEASE and exit 1. Nothing is fetched or published.
7. Release: WT-10's release_land_lease / Release-MoeLandLease runs on every exit, including the EXIT trap and the PowerShell finally.
8. Outcome and evidence:
   - Exit 0: MOE_MIGRATION_LANDED (prints the branch, target, B and C) or MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT. Nothing-to-commit means the branch tip is an ancestor of the fetched B.
   - Exit 1: every other refusal or failure.
   - No Candidate, CheckRun, ledger, journal or rescue row, and no finalize_attempt or announce.
   - The freeze and gate helpers get an explicit no-evidence opt-out; existing callers are unchanged.
9. Known daemon behaviour, accepted:
   - A queued grant passes over a row no live seat holds (grantNextLeases, heldByLiveSeat). A queued migration is therefore admitted at its next wait_for_resource re-entry, through the direct grant.
   - The 5-min reaper drops a lease whose row leaves PLANNING/WORKING/REVIEW/BLOCKED.
   - Safety never depends on the lease: CAS plus a non-forced push.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A human runs `scripts/moe-agent.sh --land-branch <branch>` or `scripts/moe-agent.ps1 -LandBranch <branch>` from the control checkout. The wrapper lands that branch on main as one gated merge commit C through the existing worktree landing core: L4 sync, L5 merge-tree of the fetched main B and the branch tip, L6 gate on exactly M in the .moe-free gate worktree, L7 commit-tree without hooks, L9 CAS or non-forced push, and L10 mirror, in at most 2 rounds. It takes no lease, sends no daemon RPC, claims nothing, and records no Candidate, CheckRun, ledger, journal or rescue entry. With no configured gate (or with MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE=1) it refuses with MOE_MIGRATION_NO_GATE before any fetch. A rerun after a publication exits 0 with MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT.
invariants: main moves only through the update-ref CAS or a non-forced push of a C whose tree M passed the gate in the same round; no push ever uses --force, -f, --force-with-lease or a '+' refspec.
C has tree M and exactly two parents, B first and the branch tip second; the source branch ref never moves.
Migration mode sends no RPC through the proxy or moe-call.sh: no lease, claim, join, get_context, evidence, ledger, finalize, chat or deregister call.
A failed, refused or unconfirmed publication never prints MOE_MIGRATION_LANDED, never moves the local target, and exits non-zero.
Shared mode and the worktree completion arm keep their behaviour; the held-out worktree-landing tests stay byte-unchanged.
moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 emit the same MOE_MIGRATION_, MOE_LAND_ and MOE_PUSH_ codes.
compatibility: Existing callers of freeze_candidate, run_frozen_gate and Invoke-MoeFrozenGate pass no new argument and behave identically; the no-evidence option is opt-in.
Every existing wrapper option and the default (non-migration) launch path are unchanged.
reuse: WT-08's merge-tree helper and local CAS publication, plus WT-09's push and reconcile_push/Resolve-MoePushOutcome.
freeze_candidate/New-MoeFrozenCandidate and run_frozen_gate worktree/Invoke-MoeFrozenGate -WorktreeMode (WT-10G/WT-10), with a new opt-in no-evidence switch.
The raw configured-qualityGate reader and the target-checked-out guard from the worktree completion arm.
postflight-owner-guard.cjs's shared-suite pattern for the new postflight-migration.cjs.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) --lease-task identity: a real operator row plus the wrapper's worker id. This planner posted it briefly and withdrew it after finding the producer's comment-5957b3a6 on WT-16 and the row author's comment-0e698959, which both say no lease. During the drained migration a lease adds nothing beyond the CAS and the non-forced push, and it would have added a flag, a runbook row and daemon edge cases: queued grants pass over unheld rows, and the reaper drops leases on rows outside the active columns. 2) A wrapper-created or claimed task: rejected. DoD 2 forbids incidental claims, and create_task makes a BACKLOG row that the reaper treats as ineligible. 3) A daemon system-owner lease: rejected, because it broadens the resource API. 4) Chosen: WT-S §7.3 in 6285adf7, no lease and no RPC, with DoD 3 pinned by the TASK rail proposal prop-46a25cec. 5) The target is fixed to `main` rather than resolveWorktreeTarget: the migration runs before consolidationBranch is set, and a literal consolidationBranch could even equal the source branch. 6) Nothing-to-commit uses WT-08's L5 rule, M == B^{tree}, which covers 'tip already contained'. 7) One shared suite file, following postflight-owner-guard.cjs, instead of two inline copies, to stay under 400 LOC. A tripwire proxy written at runtime replaces fake-proxy edits and proves 'no RPC at all' mechanically.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Evidence RPCs to skip: sh freeze_candidate calls record_candidate_rpc and run_frozen_gate calls record_check_run_rpc; ps1 Invoke-MoeFrozenGate calls Send-MoeCheckRun.

completionSummary:
WT-10M adds the gated migration landing CLI to both wrappers: `moe-agent.sh --land-branch <b>` and `moe-agent.ps1 -LandBranch <b>`.
- It lands a branch on main as ONE merge commit C, with tree M = merge-tree(B, tip) and parents exactly [B, tip].
- M always passes the .moe-free frozen gate (noevidence), whatever the scope, and there are at most 2 rounds.
- Publication is a non-forced `push --porcelain origin C:refs/heads/main` with reconcile, or a local update-ref CAS with an ancestry check.
- It takes no lease and sends no RPC. It writes no journal, rescue ref, Candidate, CheckRun or ledger row, and the source branch never moves.
